Hi Hannah / Ben,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — we’re moving to the security review stage. Attached is our security questionnaire (Nimbus_Security_Questionnaire_v3.xlsx). The compliance team has two immediate asks we need answered in writing for procurement:

1) Confirm where customer request payloads and generated content reside geographically for the hosted API, and whether we can lock to US-only.
2) Provide a documented timeline and evidence of complete deletion including backups after a customer requests a data erasure. Procurement expects a maximum daylight-to-purge number.
3) Explain retention of metadata, diagnostic logs, and model telemetry and whether those are subject to the same purge.
4) Clarify behavior for embeddings/indexes — are those persisted by default and what TTLs apply?

Can you please reply with a short, evidence-backed response we can attach to the procurement packet? We also need an "evidence bundle" (sample manifest, deletion logs, and a point of contact) for our auditors.

Appreciate a response by EOD PT today if possible.

Thanks,

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Reed <samantha.reed@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Hosted API — Residency & Deletion (detailed answers)

Samantha — following up with the technical answers and evidence notes below. I’ve tried to keep this brief and actionable; happy to hop on a call if you prefer.

High level
- Hosted API supports region pinning: requests may be routed to US-only or EU-only clusters; for your account we can enforce US-only processing and storage for all production traffic. Region pinning is enforced at the routing layer and tied to the account config (not per-request).
- All customer data (request payloads, generated output, and user-provided artifacts) is encrypted at rest using provider-managed KMS keys scoped per-region. Network in transit is TLS 1.2+; we also support customer-managed keys on Private deployments — for hosted we use AWS KMS with dedicated key aliases per region.

Retention, deletion and backups (evidence-oriented)
- Application-layer retention: by default, primary request/response artifacts for hosted API are retained for 30 days. This default is configurable per-account during onboarding (options: ephemerality from 0 to 90 days).
- Embeddings/indexes: embeddings are not stored permanently by default. Persisted embeddings require explicit opt-in; when enabled, an account-level TTL is applied (commonly 30/90/365 days) and each index has a deletion lifecycle you can set via the console or API.
- Cache/KV: transient caches (KV + prefix caches) live in memory or ephemeral SSDs and are evicted according to workload policies; their default live window is ~2 hours and they are not present in long-term backups.
- Backups and snapshots: nightly snapshots are taken of primary stores for disaster recovery. Snapshots are incremental; snapshot retention is 30 days by default. If a deletion is requested, data is removed from primary stores immediately (see timeline below) but may remain in prior snapshots until those snapshots age out or are rotated.

Deletion timeline (how we purge and evidence we can provide)
- Step 1 — Initiation: Upon a verified account erasure request, data is removed from primary production stores within 24 hours. This is a logical delete (records flagged and removed from active indexes and query paths).
- Step 2 — Secure purge queue: Deleted records are added to a secure purge queue; background jobs perform cryptographic shredding/overwrite of files on a rolling basis. This process completes in the normal case within 72 hours for active partitions.
- Step 3 — Snapshot expiry: Any prior snapshot containing the data will be removed according to the snapshot retention window (max 30 days by default). For customers requiring aggressive purge windows, we can offer a 7-day snapshot retention SLA as part of an enterprise contract.
- Evidence artifacts provided: manifest of deleted object keys (S3 paths), deletion job IDs and timestamps, checksum of removed objects, and a signed statement from Redwood security. We can deliver a sample evidence bundle (PDF + CSV + S3 manifest) for your auditors.

Logs, telemetry and audit trails
- Diagnostic logs (request metadata, errors) are retained for 90 days by default; these are stored separately from request payloads and can be configured. Telemetry used for model improvement is pseudonymized and aggregated; we offer opt-out for telemetry collection at the account level.
- Immutable audit trail: deletion requests and administrative actions are recorded in an append-only audit log for 365 days. The log records who initiated deletion, the job IDs, and the timestamp of completion. We can include sanitized audit log excerpts in the evidence bundle.

Legal holds and exceptions
- Legal holds override deletion workflows. If a legal hold is in place we will retain data until the hold is lifted and provide notice to the customer with timestamps and rationale.

Operational notes and controls
- Data export: customers can request an export (JSON/CSV) of their data. We commit to delivering exports within 72 hours of a verified request.
- Third-party auditor evidence: we can provide an S3 manifest and signed hash file that your auditors or a third-party assessor can verify.
- Certifications: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified; we can provide the relevant audit report under NDA.

Attachments: residency_matrix_2028-09-07.pdf

Next steps
- If you confirm a required maximum purge window (e.g., 30 days), we’ll generate a tailored statement and evidence template and return it this afternoon. If your auditors require shorter snapshot retention, we can propose a contractual SLA change.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Director, Security Assurance | Redwood Inference

Thanks Irene — that level of detail is helpful. A couple quick clarifications for procurement:

- When you say "removed from primary stores within 24 hours" — does that mean the data is overwritten (crypto-shredded) or logically deleted and then picked up by the purge queue you described? Please confirm whether any retained snapshot copies are considered "in-scope" for our 30-day purge requirement.
- For embeddings that were opt-ed in historically, will deletion of an account remove the indexes immediately or is there an index rebuild/compaction window where deleted vectors could persist?

If you can confirm both items in writing we’ll mark the questionnaire as tentatively approved pending the evidence bundle.

Best,
Samantha

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 8 Sep 2028 15:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API — Residency & Deletion (detailed answers)

Hi Samantha — quick confirmation from the account side and a formal statement we will include in the evidence bundle:

1) Deletion semantics: a verified deletion request triggers immediate removal from primary production stores (logical delete) within 24 hours. The secure purge queue then triggers cryptographic shredding/overwrite tasks; typical completion for active partitions is within 72 hours. We will supply deletion job IDs and completion timestamps as part of the evidence bundle so your auditors can verify the purge operations.

2) Snapshots: prior snapshots that include the deleted data are treated as recoverable DR artifacts and will be rotated out according to snapshot retention. By default that window is 30 days. If Nimbus requires a contractual 30-day absolute purge (no snapshot retention beyond X days), we can offer a 7-day snapshot retention SLA as an enterprise addendum. Please note legal holds will prevent snapshot deletion while the hold is active.

3) Embeddings/indexes: when embeddings are persisted and then deleted, the index is marked and compacted; index compaction runs on a rolling schedule but the indexing layer will stop returning deleted vectors immediately. In practice, vector entries are not available for retrieval post-deletion and compaction completes within the snapshot window (<= 30 days). We can provide a sample index compaction job log and vector deletion manifest.

Attached is a short certification we can sign and add to the procurement packet. Let us know if you want the evidence bundle in a ZIP or an S3 manifest with pre-signed URLs.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
